subject: Private deploy: BYOK high-availability, key failover decision log

Subject: BYOK HA and failover needs for private deployment

Hi Marissa / Karthik,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. MedSys is pushing a requirement into our procurement checklist: during a rollout to our staging VPC we need a documented key availability strategy for BYOK-backed model keys that meets our RTO/RPO expectations. High level asks:

- Demonstrate how key material remains available during a single-region HSM outage (operator failure or host loss).
- Show how key rotation (monthly) can be performed with zero file-serving downtime for inference pods.
- Provide a table of required network ports, firewall rules, and bastion patterns for key replication and attestation.

I've attached our requirements PDF and a skeleton rotation simulation plan. Can Redwood provide a design decision log that spells out tradeoffs (active-active proxy vs. read-only replicas, split custody vs. escrow) and a recommended playbook for the cutover?

Goal: have a decision log and a simulation runbook by Oct 27 so our security/compliance can sign off before procurement.

Alice
Security Engineering Lead
MedSys Health

Attachments: medsys-byo-requirements-20261020.pdf, rotation-sim-plan.xlsx

Alice — thanks, this is clear and reasonable. Karthik and I will own the decision log; Soojin and Olga will help with the simulation and the networking appendix. Quick clarifications before we start the write-up:

1) Do you require customer-managed HSMs (on-prem) only, or are you open to Redwood-hosted HSM peer replicas inside your VPC?
2) For rotation: is your SLA window 5 minutes of acceptable token-drop (i.e., some TCP retries), or must it be fully seamless at the application layer?
3) Any restrictions on outbound attestation endpoints from your VPC (we usually use attestation.redwood.com:443 or a signed CSR exchange over SFTP)?

If you confirm, we'll produce: decision log (MD), network rules appendix (CSV), and a runbook (XLSX) with exact steps to run a canary rotation and a forced failover drill. Expect an initial draft by Monday (Oct 26).

— Marissa
Director, Product & Security - Redwood Inference

Marissa — apologies for the late reply. Short answers:
1) We need customer-managed HSM in our primary datacenter, but we are open to Redwood-managed read-only replicas in the second AZ if the design keeps key unwrapping enforceable only inside the MedSys control plane.
2) Rotation must be seamless at the application layer; medically-critical inference flows cannot return 5xx for patient-facing requests.
3) Outbound attestation endpoints: must be limited to allowlist; attestation.redwood.com is fine if we can provide static IP ranges and a signed certificate fingerprint.

I'll add these to the requirements doc; feel free to proceed.

— Alice

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 24 Oct 2026 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: draft decision log and proposed pattern

Team — initial position below, prepping for the doc we send to MedSys. Comments inline please.

Decision summary (proposed):
- Primary key material generates and stays in customer HSM (on-prem).
- Redwood will deploy a read-only key-proxy in MedSys secondary AZ that can fetch wrapped keys but never perform unwrapping locally; unwrapping is performed by the customer HSM via secure attestation call.
- For HA we recommend a warm-standby proxy pair (active passive) + automatic DNS failover. Active-active unwrapping is not acceptable given MedSys custody requirement unless split-custody is implemented (adds ops and legal complexity).

Tradeoffs:
- Active-passive with DNS failover = simpler, predictable RPO; requires fast DNS TTL and health checks.
- Read-only replicas reduce blast radius but add latency on cold cache misses.
- Split-custody (threshold signing) would provide active-active availability but requires key-splitting hardware & legal agreements — longer lead time.

Network notes to include in appendix:
- Ports: 443 (attestation), 22 for SFTP evidence exchange (admin-only), 10250 for kubelet->proxy where needed, high-level NAT64 rules for egress.
- Required IPs (Redwood): 34.102.45.12/32, 34.102.45.13/32 (we'll confirm dedicated egress ranges).

Next actions:
- Soojin: write the rotation simulation steps (see attached template).
- Olga: produce a minimal firewall/route table example for GCP/AWS VPC peering.
- Marissa: finalize decision log and send to Alice for approval Monday AM.

Karthik

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Alice Jenkins <alice.jenkins@medsys.com>
Date: Sun, 25 Oct 2026 08:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: BYOK HA and failover needs for private deployment — draft runbook attached

Alice / team — attaching the rotation simulation runbook and a short network appendix. Key points we included in the runbook:

- Canary rotation flow: provision next key in HSM, publish wrapped key to Redwood proxy cache, switch a canary service mesh subset to use new key, monitor error rates and latency for 5 minutes, then roll forward.
- Failover drill: simulate primary HSM outage (network partition), promote warm proxy via DNS failover + a signed attestation handshake to the secondary HSM proxy; measure end-to-end latency and error rate.
- Safety net: automatic fallback to non-BYOK signed tokens (short TTL) is possible for non-critical API paths only; we marked patient-facing endpoints as non-fallback.

Notes for MedSys: the runbook requires two maintenance windows for full rehearsal (rotation + failover) and a short peering change for low TTL DNS.

Attachments included: rotation-sim-plan.xlsx, draft-decision-log.md

— Soojin
Senior Reliability Engineer — Redwood Inference

1) Can Redwood provide a short table listing maximum expected additional request latency during a cold cache miss on proxy read-only fetch (p50/p95)? We need numbers for our performance budget.
2) For the attestation endpoint IPs: please confirm the egress ranges rather than single IPs so we can add them to our allowlist.

If you can provide those by EOD Monday we'll aim to approve and attach the decision log to our procurement ticket.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

— Alice
Security Engineering Lead, MedSys Health
